MAPED v. Yangjiang Bonly Trade Co., Ltd. and Yangjiang Yilida Knife & Scissors Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of design patent

【Ruling Summary】

When determining the scope of protection of a design patent and making an infringement determination, the basic elements of shape, pattern, and color as shown in the drawings or photographs shall serve as the fundamental basis.

If a product of the same or similar kind as the design patent product adopts a design that is identical or similar to the design patent, the people's court shall find that the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the design patent. If the accused infringing product, while adopting a design identical or similar to the design patent, additionally incorporates other pattern or color design elements, and if these additional design elements are merely superfluous, they generally do not have a material impact on the infringement determination.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2013) Min Shen Zi No. 29

Retrial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): MAPED. Domicile: 530 Route de la Gilonne, Agneaux, Republic of France.

Legal Representative: Jacques Lacroix, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xiaoling, lawyer of Beijing Wanhuida Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Han, lawyer of Beijing Wanhuida Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yangjiang Bonly Trade Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 703, Building E, No. 168 Dongfeng Third Road, Jiangcheng District, Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Huang Changxi, General Manager of the company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yangjiang Yilida Knife & Scissors Co., Ltd. Domicile: Fengmen Middle School, Gangqiao District, Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Huang Changxi, General Manager of the company.

The Retrial Applicant MAPED, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2011) Yue Gao Fa Min San Zhong Zi No. 164 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in the case of dispute over infringement of design patent with the Respondents Yangjiang Bonly Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bonly Company) and Yangjiang Yilida Knife & Scissors Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yilida Company), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review the case, and the review has now been concluded.

MAPED applied to this Court for retrial, alleging: (1) A design patent of the pure shape type should receive full and effective legal protection. The judgment of the second instance, which found that the accused infringing product was neither identical nor similar to the patent in suit, did not comply with the provisions of Article 59, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) and its legislative purpose. a. The judgment of the second instance found that "the design of colored patterns on the scissor blades generally has a greater impact on the overall visual effect of the design. Judging from the knowledge level and cognitive ability of the average consumer, the above differences on the scissor blades between the infringing design and the patented design have already constituted a material difference in overall visual effect, therefore they are neither identical nor similar." This finding was erroneous in fact and improperly applied the law. b. When determining the scope of protection of a design patent of the pure shape type and judging whether the accused infringing product infringes, the provisions of Part IV, Chapter 5, Section 5.2.3 of the Patent Examination Guidelines should be applied mutatis mutandis, and the elements of pattern and color should not be considered. The pattern and color elements added to the appearance of the accused infringing product should be disregarded. c. The patent in suit is a design patent of the pure shape type, representing a fundamental innovation in product appearance, with greater difficulty in innovation, and thus should enjoy a broader scope of protection and receive more comprehensive legal protection. Therefore, as long as the accused infringing product adopts a product shape identical or similar to the patent in suit, it should be found to fall within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. d. While copying the product shape of the patent in suit, the accused infringing product intentionally added patterns to the product surface, thereby both exploiting the innovative achievements of the patentee in suit and evading infringement liability. (2) The accused infringing product constitutes an identical or similar design to the patent in suit and falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. a. Except that the rivet size of the accused infringing product is slightly larger, all other shape elements are identical to those of the patent in suit. Applying the method of overall observation and comprehensive assessment, the change in rivet size is a minor local variation, and the patent in suit and the accused infringing product are identical or similar products. b. Analyzed from the parts that are readily observable during normal use of the product, the accused infringing design falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. (3) While producing and selling the accused infringing products bearing patterns and colors, the Respondents also produced, sold, and offered for sale products of model SC0306 that did not bear patterns or colors and were completely identical to the patent in suit. Page 36 of the "2008 Yangjiang Bonly Products Catalog Yangjiang Bonly Industries LTD PROFESSIONAL SCISSORS FACTORY" printed and distributed by Bonly Company records that the scissor blades of the SC0306 scissors are colorless metal. The accused infringing products alleged by MAPED in the first and second instances included products without patterns or colors. The court of first instance did not examine and find this, thus the finding of fact was erroneous. (4) Bonly Company and Yilida Company jointly committed the infringing acts and should jointly bear the legal liability for ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses. The reasonable expenses incurred by MAPED to stop the infringing acts should be borne by Yilida Company. In summary, MAPED applied to this Court for retrial in accordance with Article 179, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2007). It requested this Court to: 1. Set aside the judgments of the first and second instances. 2. Order Bonly Company and Yilida Company to cease the acts infringing the patent in suit and to pay RMB 100,000 in damages for economic losses.

Bonly Company and Yilida Company did not submit defense opinions.

This Court finds that the focal points of this case are: 1. Whether the court of first instance omitted the accused infringing products without patterns or colors. 2. Whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the design patent in suit. 3. What effect the colored patterns on the blades of the accused infringing product have on the infringement determination.

I. Whether the Court of First Instance Omitted the Accused Infringing Products Without Patterns or Colors

Upon examination, this Court finds that MAPED did not assert in the first instance that Bonly Company and Yilida Company produced or sold accused infringing products without patterns or designs on the blades. According to the trial transcript of the first instance and the written opinions submitted by MAPED, when making the infringement comparison, MAPED expressly stated that "the only differences between the two are the difference in rivet size and that the accused infringing product has patterns and colors printed on the blades. ... The accused infringing product is similar to the patent in suit." Therefore, MAPED's assertion that the court of first instance omitted the accused infringing products lacks factual basis and is not supported by this Court.

II. Whether the Accused Infringing Product Falls Within the Scope of Protection of the Design Patent in Suit

Comparing the accused infringing product with the design patent in suit, both include three main parts: the handle, the blade, and the rivet set in the middle of the scissors. The commonalities are that the shapes of the handles and blades are essentially the same, the handle includes two concentric rings of different brightness (light and dark), and there is a water-drop shaped through-hole in the middle of the handle. The main differences are: 1. The rivet of the accused infringing product is two truncated-cone-shaped protrusions respectively set on both sides of the scissors, noticeably larger in volume, with wavy stripes on its centerline; the rivet of the patent in suit is a metal rivet, noticeably smaller in volume, with only a straight groove on one side in the middle (hereinafter referred to as Difference 1). 2. The scissor blades of the accused infringing product also have colored patterns (hereinafter referred to as Difference 2).

Regarding Difference 1: For the design patent in suit, the designs of the blade and rivet are both conventional designs in scissor products, with the design characteristics mainly reflected in the handle, and the height of innovation is relatively limited. Although the accused infringing product adopts a handle design essentially the same as the patent in suit, due to the obvious differences in the shape and size of the rivets, and because the rivet is set in the middle of the product, Difference 1 is easily observable by the average consumer and is sufficient to cause a clear difference in the overall visual effect between the two.

Regarding Difference 2: First, correctly defining the scope of protection of a design patent is the basis for making an infringement determination for a design patent. According to Article 56, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2000), "the scope of protection of a design patent shall be determined based on the product incorporating the patented design as shown in the drawings or photographs." Shape, pattern, and color are the three basic design elements constituting a product's appearance design. Therefore, when determining the scope of protection of a design patent and making an infringement determination, the design elements of shape, pattern, and color as shown in the drawings or photographs shall serve as the fundamental basis. Second, the element of color cannot exist independently of shape and pattern; it must be attached to the product's shape and pattern, and changes in color themselves can also form patterns. According to Article 28, Paragraph 2 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2002), "the brief explanation of the design shall state the design points of the product using the design, the request for protection of color, omitted views, and other matters." Therefore, if the brief explanation does not expressly request protection of color, the color in the drawings or photographs shall not be used to limit the scope of protection of the design patent and shall be disregarded in the infringement comparison. However, patterns formed by variations in brightness and shade on the product shall be considered as pattern design elements, not as color design elements. The concentric rings of different brightness on the handle of the patent in suit are pattern design elements. MAPED's assertion that the patent in suit is a design of the pure shape type is inconsistent with the facts. Finally, if a product of the same or similar kind as the design patent product adopts a design that is identical or similar to the design patent, the people's court shall find that the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the design patent as provided in Article 59, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law. If the accused infringing product, while adopting a design identical or similar to the design patent, additionally incorporates other pattern or color design elements, and if these additional design elements are merely superfluous, they generally do not have a material impact on the infringement determination. Otherwise, others could easily circumvent patent infringement by simply adding patterns or colors to the design patent. This would undoubtedly contravene the legislative intent of the Patent Law to encourage invention and creation and to promote technological progress and innovation. The patent in suit does not request protection of color, nor does it have pattern designs on the blades. Difference 2 is an additional design element on the accused infringing product and should not have a material impact on the infringement determination.

In summary, Difference 1 has a significant impact on the overall visual effect, and the accused infringing product is neither identical nor similar to the design patent in suit. The judgment of the second instance, on grounds including "the design of colored patterns on the scissor blades generally has a greater impact on the overall visual effect of the design," found that the overall visual effects of the two had a material difference. This application of law was erroneous and should be corrected. Since the conclusion of the second instance judgment was correct, this Court affirms it.

Accordingly, the retrial application of MAPED does not satisfy the conditions set forth in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The retrial application of MAPED is rejected.

Presiding Judge: Zhou Xiang

Acting Judge: Du Weike

Acting Judge: Luo Xia
